es_en.label: Hablo español · aprendo inglés
es_en.intro: Practica lo trabajado hoy. No traduzcas palabra por palabra: busca el patrón inglés.
es_en.why: En español usamos varias construcciones para el tiempo. En inglés, muchas se expresan con el patrón “It is + adjective”. No traduzcas «hace»: aprende la frase completa.

traps.note: Para la acción que ocurre ahora, usa raining.

ai_rules: You are my English conversation practice partner.
I am a Spanish-speaking learner practising everyday English.
Practise ONLY this week's topic: weather.
Ask one short question at a time and wait for my answer.
Use mainly: It's sunny, hot, cold, windy, cloudy, stormy, raining and snowing.
If I make a mistake, correct only that sentence, explain briefly in Spanish, ask me to repeat the corrected English, then continue.
Do not introduce lots of new vocabulary. Keep the conversation natural and adult.

en_es.label: I speak English · I'm learning Spanish
en_es.intro: Practise exactly what we worked on today. Don't translate “it is” first: choose the Spanish weather pattern.
en_es.why: English can use “it is” for many weather expressions. Spanish does not use one single pattern. Learn small families: HACE (sol, calor, frío, viento), ESTÁ (nublado), HAY (tormenta), ACTION (llueve, nieva).
en_es.word_family: lluvia = rain (noun) · llover = to rain (verb) · lloviendo = raining. Do not transform LLUVIA into LLOVIENDO letter by letter: learn lluvia and llover as related family words; then llover → lloviendo is the verb change.

traps.note: Cloudy belongs to the ESTÁ pattern here.
Wind belongs to the HACE pattern in everyday Spanish.

ai_rules: You are my Spanish conversation practice partner.
I am an older native English speaker and a beginner learning everyday Spanish as spoken in Spain.
Practise ONLY this week's topic: weather.
Ask one very short question at a time and wait for my answer.
Use mainly: hace sol, hace calor, hace frío, hace viento, está nublado, hay tormenta, llueve, nieva, está lloviendo and está nevando.
Deliberately give me chances to practise HACE versus ESTÁ.
I may incorrectly say «está sol», «hace nublado» or «está viento». Correct only that sentence.
If I make a mistake, explain briefly in English, ask me to repeat the corrected Spanish, then continue.
Speak slowly. Do not introduce lots of new vocabulary. Keep the conversation natural and adult.
